memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Listen now to me and I will give you some advice, and may God be with you. You
must be the people's representative before God and bring their disputes to him.
Teach them his decrees and instructions, and show them the way they are to live
and how they are to behave." - Ex 18:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jethro does not simply criticise. He offers a plan, and the plan begins by naming
what Moses must keep.

Notice the order. Before he says what to delegate, he says what is
irreplaceable. Moses must stand before God for the people. He must teach them.
He must show them how to live.

That is wise counsel. When we are overloaded, the temptation is to cut whatever
is easiest to cut, which is often the most important thing. Prayer goes first
because nobody notices immediately. Teaching gets thinner. The urgent crowds out
the essential.

Jethro protects the core. Keep the prayer. Keep the teaching. Delegate the rest.

The apostles made exactly this judgment when the early church grew too fast for
them. They appointed others to handle the daily distribution so they could
"give our attention to prayer and the ministry of the word" (Acts 6:4). That was
not laziness or a claim to superiority. It was clarity about what only they could
do.

Notice also Jethro's tone: "may God be with you." He gives advice, not commands,
and he blesses Moses in the giving of it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What is the one thing in your responsibilities that only you can do?
2. When you get busy, what is the first thing you drop?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me to see clearly what is mine to carry and what is not. Guard the
most important things from being squeezed out. Amen.
